$comment: THE PHOTOGRAPH LICENCE GATE. No verified licence, no production image. Each of the three facts must be answered with a VERBATIM QUOTE and the URL it came from, and checks.py asserts that quote appears in the archived snapshot of that page under provider-terms/. That is the point: an answer cannot be typed from memory, because the evidence has to exist in the repository beside it. Run scripts/images/verify_provider.py to fetch and archive the live terms; it cannot run in the sandbox, whose egress proxy blocks both providers — which is exactly why the gate exists rather than a recollection.
$schema_note: Each of self_host, attribution, download_ping is {value, quote, source}. value: self_host true/false, attribution a string, download_ping true/false. quote: copied verbatim from the page. source: the URL. UNANSWERED anywhere means STOP.

self_host.question: May the file be downloaded and served from europedoor.com? This site sends `img-src 'self' data:` and checks.py refuses any third-party origin, so a provider that requires hotlinking cannot be used without an owner decision that changes both.
self_host.quote: All photos and videos on Pexels can be downloaded and used for free.

attribution.value: A prominent link to Pexels on any page showing a Pexels photo, and the photographer credited as “Photo by <name> on Pexels” linking to that photo’s page on Pexels.
attribution.question: The EXACT credit the terms require. picture() prints `<photographer> · <licence>`. If a link to the provider or to the photographer's profile or specific wording is required, the renderer changes BEFORE the first fetch.
attribution.quote: Whenever you are doing an API request make sure to show a prominent link to Pexels. You can use a text link (e.g. "Photos provided by Pexels") or a link with our logo. Always credit our photographers when possible (e.g. "Photo by John Doe on Pexels" with a link to the photo page on Pexels).

download_ping.question: Does using an image require a request to a separate endpoint? If yes, set endpoint_download.
download_ping.quote: You may not copy or replicate core functionality of Pexels (including making Pexels content available as a wallpaper app). Do not abuse the API. By default, the API is rate-limited to 200 requests per hour and 20,000 requests per month.
download_ping.basis: The API documentation's Guidelines section is where Pexels states what a consumer must do per request, and it names two obligations — a prominent link and photographer credit — and no event endpoint. No endpoint in the documentation tracks a download: the photo endpoints are search, curated and photos/:id, and the Photo resource carries no download-tracking link. Compare Unsplash, whose documentation has a `Track a photo download` endpoint and says outright that you must call it.

unsplash.$warning: AN ASSISTANT'S RECOLLECTION ABOUT THIS PROVIDER IS NOT A FACT AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS ONE. There is a suspicion on record that the API guidelines require using the hotlinked URLs returned under photo.urls, require crediting both the photographer and Unsplash with links, and require triggering a download endpoint on use. Every one of those is a SUSPICION. It exists here only so somebody knows what to look for on the page, and it may not be copied into `value` without the quote that supports it.

self_host.question: Same question, and the one to read closely for this provider. Answer from the live guidelines, never from the warning above.
self_host.quote: All API uses must use the hotlinked image URLs returned by the API under the `photo.urls`  properties. This applies to all uses of the image and not just search results.
self_host.basis: The licence page says images may be downloaded and used freely, and the API guidelines say API consumers must embed Unsplash's own URLs. Both are true and the narrower one binds anything fetched through the API, which is how this pipeline would fetch.

attribution.value: Unsplash and the photographer must both be named, with a link back to the photographer’s Unsplash profile carrying ?utm_source=<app>&utm_medium=referral.
attribution.question: As above. If both the photographer and the provider must be credited with links, picture() needs a second link before anything ships.
attribution.quote: When displaying a photo from Unsplash, your application must attribute Unsplash, the Unsplash photographer, and contain a link back to their Unsplash profile.

download_ping.question: If a download endpoint must be triggered on use, set endpoint_download and fetch.py will call it.
download_ping.quote: When your application performs something similar to a download (like when a user chooses the image to include in a blog post, set as a header, etc.), you must send a request to the download endpoint returned under the `photo.links.download_location`  property.

unsplash.unusable_because: Unsplash requires hotlinking: images must be served from its own CDN rather than from this origin. EuropeDoor sends `img-src 'self' data:` and checks.py refuses any third-party origin on any page, so honouring that means opening the Content-Security-Policy on all 1,033 pages to a host we do not control. That is a decision about the security posture of the whole site and belongs to the owner, not to a build step. Pexels requires no such thing, so the photograph pipeline uses Pexels and this row stays closed with its reading recorded.
